## Hosted reproduction and exact scope
PR #189 at `463f2cc6fd2957c6a853268a2ce16fb34dce34d1` fails the retained complete-local-corpus dry-run regression on both supported Node versions:
- [Node 22](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/actions/runs/40921539271/job/123615778899)
- [Node 26](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/actions/runs/40921539271/job/123615778739)

Each logs 444 tests, 440 passed, 4 failed. The specific test [complete-local-reads.test.ts:46–86](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/463f2cc6fd2957c6a853268a2ce16fb34dce34d1/test/complete-local-reads.test.ts#L46-L86) constructs 10,002 real SDK items and successfully exports the complete corpus. Its one-issue legacy `atomic:true,dryRun:true` sync then throws `Tracker isolation budget exceeded` at index.ts:2480, rather than returning the expected existing-item match.

## Cause and intended-contract conflict
The 20,000-filesystem-entry/64MiB physical-copy guard is deliberate, pre-existing and documented for ownership/closure reads. It must not simply be removed or weakened.

In [the earlier implementation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/75acc52aa905db1aee0c5f694f05d16b86e49c4b/index.ts#L3733-L3755), legacy atomic dry-run counted already prepared matches. The unified forward importer now sends this path through `importEstimateBatch` → `readClosureItems`, introducing the full physical-copy admission bound to that workflow. The guard counts filesystem entries, including per-item history, not logical items.

The [current complete-read promise](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/463f2cc6fd2957c6a853268a2ce16fb34dce34d1/README.md#L201-L214) includes sync/import matching and offline previews, with no 10,000-item limit. Closed [#134](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/issues/134) and its [canonical record](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/463f2cc6fd2957c6a853268a2ce16fb34dce34d1/.agents/pm/issues/pm-linear-github-18076be0368a-134.toon) explicitly require >10,000-item coverage. Current documentation does not reconcile that workflow promise with the inherited copy limit.

## Expected / actual / impact
Expected: the supported complete-corpus preview can match the existing item without truncation or unsafe source mutation, or an explicitly accepted narrower capability is disclosed with actionable admission diagnostics before work.
Actual: the previously covered preview aborts at isolation-copy admission. Full release qualification remains red. This is a deliberate safety refusal exposed on a newly widened call path, not evidence of data loss or unsafe guard behavior.

## Acceptance
- Retain source isolation, complete membership/history semantics and bounded resource use. Prefer a supported bounded/incremental shared-SDK approach if preserving the existing workflow; do not bypass the guard, truncate items/history, or repair the user's source to make tests pass.
- If the narrower admission contract is intentional, record the accepted tradeoff, distinguish item counts from physical entry/byte budgets, expose a typed actionable refusal, and reconcile the complete-read documentation and regression expectations.
- Retain deterministic >10,000-item complete export/matching coverage and separately test admitted/refused preview boundaries.
- Rerun the focused regression plus complete Node22/26/npm/Bun gates on the repaired exact head; report unrelated failures separately.

## Other current gate failures and limits
The other three assertions concern a legacy retained-assignee oracle and two identical-repeat updated-count expectations. Static inspection finds they conflict with the newly documented clearing/unchanged contracts; no production write failure is established from those assertions alone. Reconcile their intended contracts without weakening actual preservation or truthful receipts. They are not the cause of the corpus-budget refusal.

Evidence: hosted execution plus exact-source/accepted-record comparison. No local large-corpus, native/provider, security or concurrency reproduction. No npm publication claim. All-status192 issue/PR records checked: #191 covers explicit atomic-request compatibility; #188 missing-configuration reads and #184 an older coverage gate are distinct. PR189 remains implementation owner.
